dogpile_hypotheses:
### Hypothesis 1: Larger Model (bert-base-uncased)
**What:** Replace distilbert-base-uncased with bert-base-uncased (110M vs 66M params). The 0.010 gap suggests the model is capacity-limited on edge cases.
**Why:** DistilBERT sacrifices 3-5% F1 for speed on nuanced multi-class text tasks. Full BERT consistently closes small gaps.
**Expected lift:** +0.015-0.025 F1

### Hypothesis 2: Label Smoothing (0.1)
**What:** Apply label smoothing with alpha=0.1 to the cross-entropy loss. Currently using hard labels.
**Why:** At F1=0.890, the model is likely overconfident on boundary samples. Label smoothing regularizes decision boundaries and improves calibration on ambiguous news articles.
**Expected lift:** +0.005-0.015 F1

### Hypothesis 3: Weighted Sampling for Class Imbalance
**What:** Apply inverse-frequency class weights to the sampler. AG News has slight imbalance between World/Sports vs Sci/Tech/Business.
**Why:** Macro F1 penalizes weak classes. If Sci/Tech has fewer samples, weighted sampling ensures equal representation per batch.
**Expected lift:** +0.005-0.010 F1

### Hypothesis 4: Learning Rate Warmup + Cosine Decay
**What:** Add 10% warmup steps with cosine annealing instead of constant LR. Current LR schedule may overshoot fine-tuning optima.
**Why:** Transformers are sensitive to early LR — warmup prevents catastrophic forgetting of pretrained features. Cosine decay finds flatter minima.
**Expected lift:** +0.003-0.008 F1

### Hypothesis 5: Sentence-Transformers Backbone
**What:** Try sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 as the feature extractor with a classification head. Different embedding space may capture topic semantics better.
**Why:** Sentence-level embeddings are trained on diverse semantic similarity tasks — may generalize better across news topic boundaries than token-level BERT.
**Expected lift:** +0.010-0.020 F1
